rules.title: Assumption traceability
rules.statement: Every assumption retains its source, transformation, affected claim, and replacement condition.

rules.title: Preserve original values
rules.statement: A calculation retains every original value and unit separately from normalized or computed values.

rules.title: Exact claim evidence binding
rules.statement: Every scientific claim binds the smallest sufficient accepted evidence locators and their content identities.

rules.title: Method and scope claim ceiling
rules.statement: A conclusion cannot exceed the accepted method, system boundary, evidence coverage, and uncertainty basis.

rules.title: Permission boundary
rules.statement: Evidence access or protocol connectivity never grants authority to write, publish, pay, or change accepted project truth.

rules.title: Comparative claim ceiling
rules.statement: A comparative preference is prohibited when functional equivalence, boundary, method, coverage, or uncertainty remains non-equivalent.

rules.title: Common method basis
rules.statement: Compared alternatives use the same LCIA method, indicator definitions, temporal basis, and characterization coverage or disclose the mismatch.

rules.title: Functional equivalence
rules.statement: Compared alternatives provide an explicitly equivalent function, functional unit, reference flow, and system boundary.

rules.title: Data gap claim ceiling
rules.statement: Unresolved material data gaps lower the conclusion to the strongest explicitly bounded statement supported by remaining evidence.

rules.title: Data gap ownership
rules.statement: A missing datum identifies whether it is user-owned, source-researchable, tool-computable, or unavailable before routing.

rules.title: Exact flow identity
rules.statement: Flow matching preserves exact flow, flow-property, unit-group, direction, provider, and version identities rather than names alone.

rules.title: Functional unit completeness
rules.statement: A functional unit states the quantified function, amount, unit, performance conditions, and reference flow required by the intended use.

rules.title: System boundary completeness
rules.statement: A system boundary declares included life-cycle stages, exclusions, cut-off rules, allocation, geography, time, and technology scope.

rules.title: Interpretation basis
rules.statement: Result interpretation retains the functional unit, boundary, inventory coverage, LCIA method, scenario, and calculation version that produced the result.

rules.title: Interpretation coverage ceiling
rules.statement: Missing exchanges, processes, impact categories, or sensitivity coverage lower the interpretation claim ceiling.

rules.title: Hotspot is not causality
rules.statement: A contribution hotspot is an accounting contribution within the modeled system and is not by itself a causal effect or intervention outcome.

rules.title: Dimensional compatibility
rules.statement: A conversion or aggregation is permitted only when flow properties and physical dimensions are compatible and the conversion factor is source-bound.

rules.title: Inventory completeness coverage
rules.statement: Inventory completeness reports covered and unresolved exchanges, providers, reference flows, cut-offs, and recursion boundaries.

rules.title: Typed exchange direction
rules.statement: Every inventory exchange retains its input or output direction, quantitative reference status, flow type, amount, and unit.

rules.title: Exact provider relation
rules.statement: A provider link binds an exact producing process and product or waste flow relation with version and quantitative-reference semantics.

rules.title: Tool-only numeric LCIA
rules.statement: Formal LCIA numeric results require an accepted deterministic calculation receipt; a model may explain but may not invent the calculation.

rules.title: Characterization coverage
rules.statement: LCIA results disclose inventory flows without characterization factors, excluded categories, regionalization gaps, and method-version coverage.

rules.title: LCIA method intended-use fit
rules.statement: An LCIA method is selected by intended use, covered indicators, geography, time, inventory compatibility, and required claim type.

rules.title: Exact TianGong object identity
rules.statement: A TianGong claim binds the official object kind, UUID, version, provider, unit, and native source identity observed by an authorized capability.

rules.title: TianGong version and temporal fit
rules.statement: A TianGong object version is admissible only when its validity, update relation, and temporal representativeness fit the research state.
